summary: Extends CalendarConnector from read-only to write-capable by upgrading the OAuth scope, adding a POST /api/calendar/events endpoint that creates events in a fixed operator-configured target calendar, and persisting a decision log record for every create attempt.

classification.why_platform: Event creation through a Google Calendar API connection is a reusable technical capability with no embedded domain meaning. The connector owns the OAuth lifecycle, credential storage, target calendar enforcement, and audit persistence. Domain decisions about what events to create remain in the calling application (Chronos skill).
non_goals: Writing to any calendar other than the operator-configured Chronos target calendar
Rich Google event features beyond minimum create payload (attendees, reminders, recurrence, conferencing)
Background sync, retry workers, or async execution
Per-user ownership or per-user calendar routing
At-rest token encryption (known gap — deferred from Sprint01)

consumes: CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID from 01_System/config.env — required deployment input; CalendarConnector raises RuntimeError at startup if absent
Google OAuth 2.0 authorization and token endpoints (external)
Google Calendar API v3 events.insert endpoint (external)
provides: GET /api/calendar/google/connect/start — initiates Google Calendar OAuth consent flow (now requests calendar read+write scope)
GET /api/calendar/google/connect/callback — receives auth code, exchanges tokens, persists connection state
GET /api/calendar/events?from=<ISO8601>&to=<ISO8601> — returns Dataset of normalized calendar events (unchanged from Sprint01)
GET /api/calendar/status — returns Dataset describing current connection health (unchanged from Sprint01)
POST /api/calendar/events — creates a new event in the operator-configured Chronos target calendar; returns structured success payload; persists decision log entry
invariants: Calendar connection state is independent of Atlas login state.
Token fields (access_token, refresh_token) are never included in any API response body.
All API error responses use the api_error() envelope from platform_errorhandling.
POST /api/calendar/events always writes to the calendar identified by CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID — never to a caller-supplied calendar ID.
POST /api/calendar/events writes a decision log entry for every create attempt, regardless of outcome.
A decision log write failure must never cause the endpoint to return an error if the Google API call succeeded.

POST /api/calendar/events requires write-capable authorization (scope: calendar). If the stored connection was granted only calendar.readonly scope, the endpoint must reject the request with INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE.
The component uses the existing GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET — no separate OAuth client.
Atlas is system-scoped: no user_id FK on any table.
OAuth scope for connect_start is now https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar (read+write superset of calendar.readonly).
Existing read endpoints (GET /api/calendar/events, GET /api/calendar/status) continue to function after scope upgrade — calendar scope is a superset of calendar.readonly.
failure_modes: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE: Stored granted_scopes does not include 'calendar' write scope — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE', status=403) with message directing operator to re-run consent flow
CALENDAR_TARGET_NOT_CONFIGURED: CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID env var is absent — service raises RuntimeError at startup (fail-fast)
CALENDAR_TARGET_NOT_FOUND: Google Calendar API returns 404 for the configured calendar ID — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='CALENDAR_TARGET_NOT_FOUND', status=502)
NO_CONNECTION: No calendar_connection record exists — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='NO_CALENDAR_CONNECTION', status=404)
CONNECTION_EXPIRED: Token is expired and refresh fails — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='CALENDAR_TOKEN_EXPIRED', status=503)
CONNECTION_REVOKED: Google revoked access — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='CALENDAR_ACCESS_REVOKED', status=503)
GOOGLE_API_ERROR: Google Calendar API returns non-2xx on insert — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='GOOGLE_API_ERROR', status=502)
INVALID_INPUT: Required fields (title, start_at, end_at) missing or malformed — POST endpoint returns api_error(code='INVALID_EVENT_INPUT', status=400)
DB_UNAVAILABLE: Database unreachable — requests fail with 500 via install_exception_handlers

new_in_sprint02: CalendarCreateEventRequest: title (string, required), start_at (ISO8601 string, required), end_at (ISO8601 string, required), description (string|null, optional), location (string|null, optional), all_day (boolean, optional, default false) — Pydantic model for POST /api/calendar/events request body

CalendarCreateEventResult: status (string, 'created'), google_event_id (string), title (string), start_at (ISO8601 string), end_at (ISO8601 string), all_day (boolean), source_calendar_id (string), source_calendar_label (string|null) — Pydantic model for POST /api/calendar/events success response

consumes: Google Calendar API v3: POST https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/{calendarId}/events (event insert)
CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID env var — resolved at startup
provides: POST /api/calendar/events -> JSONResponse (CalendarCreateEventResult as JSON) | JSONResponse api_error

exposed_surfaces.name: POST /api/calendar/events
exposed_surfaces.purpose: Validates request body (title, start_at, end_at required), checks connection and scope, inserts event into CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID calendar via Google Calendar API v3, writes decision log entry, returns success payload or api_error

changed_in_sprint02.connect_start_scope: build_authorization_url() now requests https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar (read+write) instead of https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.readonly

internal_flow.name: connect_start (updated)
internal_flow.description: Unchanged from Sprint01 except: scope changes from calendar.readonly to calendar. This is the only change to the existing connect flow. Operator must re-run this flow after deployment to upgrade the granted scope.
outputs: RedirectResponse to Google consent URL (calendar scope)

internal_flow.name: connect_callback
internal_flow.description: Unchanged from Sprint01. The expanded calendar scope is stored in granted_scopes on upsert.

internal_flow.name: token_refresh_check
internal_flow.description: Unchanged from Sprint01. Used internally before any Google API request.
outputs: Or failure mode raised: CONNECTION_EXPIRED or CONNECTION_REVOKED

internal_flow.name: fetch_events
outputs: Or api_error on any failure mode

internal_flow.name: create_event
internal_flow.description: New in Sprint02. 1) Validate request body: title, start_at, end_at required. 2) Check connection record exists. 3) Call token_refresh_check (reuse existing pattern). 4) Check granted_scopes includes write-capable scope; if not, return INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE. 5) Resolve target calendar ID from CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID env var. 6) Call Google Calendar API v3 events.insert on the target calendar. 7) Write decision log entry (best-effort — catch DB exceptions, log, do not propagate). 8) On success: return CalendarCreateEventResult as JSON 201. 9) On failure: write failure decision log entry (best-effort), return api_error.
inputs: Google Calendar API v3 insert response
outputs: Google Calendar event created in target calendar
JSONResponse api_error on any failure mode

design_decisions.decision: database.py init_schema() must be updated to run all .sql files in migrations/ sorted by filename, not only 001_init.sql by hardcoded name.
design_decisions.rationale: Current init_schema() hardcodes the path to 001_init.sql. Sprint02 adds 002_write_capability.sql. Without this change, the new table will not be created on startup. The fix is minimal: replace the hardcoded path with a sorted glob over the migrations/ directory.

design_decisions.decision: OAuth scope change from calendar.readonly to calendar requires operator re-consent.
design_decisions.rationale: Google does not automatically upgrade a previously granted scope. The operator must re-run GET /api/calendar/google/connect/start after deployment to obtain a new grant with the expanded scope. This is a deployment pre-condition, not an implementation decision.

design_decisions.decision: INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE check: verify granted_scopes contains 'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar' (not just 'calendar.readonly') before accepting POST /api/calendar/events.
design_decisions.rationale: Existing connections granted before this sprint will have calendar.readonly scope only. Attempting to write with a read-only token will fail at Google with a 403. The connector must detect this condition early and return a clear error directing the operator to re-consent.

design_decisions.decision: Decision log write is best-effort: DB exceptions are caught, logged, and not propagated to the caller.
design_decisions.rationale: The primary success criterion is that the Google event was created. A secondary audit failure must not retroactively fail a successful create operation from the caller's perspective. The operator can diagnose missing log entries from application logs.

design_decisions.decision: CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID env var validated at startup (fail-fast), not at request time.
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with how _client_id() and _client_secret() are validated in google_oauth.py. Fail-fast surfaces misconfiguration immediately at container start rather than on the first request.

design_decisions.decision: Migration runner path: init_schema() remains the authoritative schema deployment path (unchanged from Sprint01 design_decision).
design_decisions.rationale: Same rationale as Sprint01: migrate.py scans Application paths only. Extension to Platform paths remains deferred.

risks.risk: Operator does not re-run OAuth consent flow after deployment
risks.impact: POST /api/calendar/events returns INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE for all requests. Connector is functional but write capability is unavailable until re-consent is completed. Resolution: operator runs GET /api/calendar/google/connect/start and completes the Google consent screen.

risks.risk: CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID not set in config.env before deployment
risks.impact: Service fails to start (RuntimeError at startup). Resolution: operator adds the calendar ID to config.env and restarts the service.

risks.risk: Google Calendar ID for Chronos calendar unknown at design time
risks.impact: Deployment blocked until operator retrieves the calendar ID from Google Calendar settings and adds it to config.env. This is an operational input that cannot be determined from the codebase.

risks.risk: Token plaintext storage (carried forward from Sprint01)
risks.impact: access_token and refresh_token stored as plaintext in Postgres. Known gap — must be addressed before production use.

deployment_preconditions: Operator must add CALENDAR_TARGET_CALENDAR_ID=<chronos-calendar-id> to 01_System/config.env before first deployment
Operator must re-run GET /api/calendar/google/connect/start after deployment to upgrade the OAuth scope from calendar.readonly to calendar
Google Cloud Console callback URI registration (http://localhost:8021/api/calendar/google/connect/callback) must remain valid — no change from Sprint01
